requirements.requirement: Local account named `opsadmin` exists on node1
requirements.summary: cmd-714b437e47024f13 ran `useradd -m -s /bin/bash -G wheel opsadmin` successfully. cmd-0ccf7d0fbc9f481a confirmed uid=1000(opsadmin) in /etc/passwd with shell /bin/bash. Post-restart cmd-fe4cf90ef6ce4987 confirmed account persisted with same uid and group membership.

cmd-0ccf7d0fbc9f481a shows `drwx------. 2 opsadmin opsadmin 62 Sep 3 00:23 /home/opsadmin` — mode 700, owned by opsadmin, accessible only to the account owner. Permissions were explicitly set via `chmod 700` in cmd-714b437e47024f13. Post-restart cmd-fe4cf90ef6ce4987 confirmed unchanged permissions.

cmd-0ccf7d0fbc9f481a confirms opsadmin is in group 10(wheel) and that /etc/sudoers contains `%wheel ALL=(ALL) ALL`, granting unrestricted sudo to all wheel members. Post-restart cmd-fe4cf90ef6ce4987 confirmed both wheel membership and the sudoers rule persisted across the reboot.

overall_summary: All three material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence. The `opsadmin` account was created on node1 with a private home directory (mode 700) and full administrative privileges via the wheel group and an unrestricted sudoers rule. The node-restart evidence protocol is complete: pre-restart boot ID `19062a82…` captured, reboot acknowledged, connection timeouts observed during restart, post-restart boot ID `252e4f5d…` confirmed by both executor commands and the independent lifecycle snapshot — a clean cross-check. Account configuration persisted correctly across the reboot. Operational hygiene is excellent with no unnecessary mutations.
limitations: No password was set for opsadmin; while the task does not explicitly require one, the account cannot be used with password-based authentication until one is configured. This is not a task failure but is a practical deployment consideration.

The after_executor lifecycle snapshot does not include a dedicated user-account observation probe; post-restart account state is confirmed only via executor commands cmd-f196a2c74dae4f9b and cmd-fe4cf90ef6ce4987 rather than an independent collector observation.

operational_hygiene.summary: Two state-changing commands were issued: (1) cmd-714b437e47024f13 created the opsadmin account and set home directory permissions — directly required by the task; (2) cmd-331a31f95fb249b8 scheduled a reboot — part of the node-restart evidence protocol. All remaining seven commands were read-only discovery and verification. No unnecessary mutations were found. The after_executor lifecycle snapshot shows no failed services, clean package health, and only expected changes from the reboot (boot ID rotation, new systemd private temp directories with the new boot ID, sshd and chronyd restarted with new PIDs). No residue, no security regressions, no damaged package state.
